purpose: Approved T70 haunted necropolis direction; single straight modular wall concept pending visual review
generationPrompt: Use the supplied gatehouse image strictly as the material and architectural style reference. Create ONE straight, repeatable 6-meter-long fortress town wall section for the same Starhaven T70 deep-wilderness haunted necropolis, reclaimed as a functioning settlement by ghosts and friendly undead. Stylized richly hand-painted 3D asset concept, isolated on a plain light gray studio background, three-quarter front view that clearly reveals the front face, both vertical cut ends, wall thickness, and full bottom-to-top footprint with margin. The wall is a full-height opaque barrier of monumental weatherworn cracked black-violet nightglass and dark basalt blocks. Continuous level walkable parapet behind a regular crenellated outer top, with a subtle lower coping band. Sparse eroded funerary and constellation relief carved into the CENTER of the span, oxidized iron repair straps and faint teal spectral accents, grime, mineral veining, missing chips and layered age. A few old fractures and patches stay inside the span. CRITICAL modular join: left and right ends are perfectly flat vertical rectangular joining planes of exactly equal height, thickness, and profile; stone courses, base, walkway, and crenellation rhythm continue to each edge so identical copies connect flush in a straight line. Both join ends are intact and unbroken, with no decoration protruding beyond either joining plane. No towers, turrets, gate, door, windows, endcaps, pilasters at ends, returns, taper, angled wings, detached rubble, dirt/terrain base, people, text, labels, warm light, golden trim, clean storybook appearance, villain spikes, gore, or levitating parts. Make construction visually credible and proportioned to the supplied gatehouse.
editPrompt: Edit the provided wall concept as a truly seamless repeatable straight wall module. Keep its material palette, aged funerary carvings, oxidized iron, overall height, thickness, and view. Correct ONLY the modular geometry: remove the large terminal pier or endcap column at BOTH left and right ends, including its bands and base projection. Cut the wall off at two flat, vertical, parallel rectangular joining planes of identical thickness and height. Neither end may flare, taper, step outward, or project beyond the long wall face. Make the crenellation rhythm periodic: a HALF MERLON at the exact left edge and a HALF MERLON at the exact right edge, so when identical copies touch they form a full merlon with equal spacing. Continue parapet walkway and horizontal iron courses cleanly through each join plane. Keep all decay away from the terminal joining faces. Show both complete ends in a three-quarter view with generous margin. Isolated light gray studio background, no additional object or text.

visualReview.match: Cracked dark basalt/nightglass, oxidized teal iron, eroded funerary and constellation relief align with gatehouse-v2.
visualReview.repeatability: Terminal piers removed. Wall is straight with level parapet and equal-height ends. The image still depicts full merlons and detail to the edge; a 3D modeler must set an exact shared crenellation phase and flat cut plane for true seamless repetition.
visualReview.constraints: No terrain or characters; opaque lower barrier. Image is concept reference, not measured geometry.
